title: Dedicated Capacity: Capacity Guarantees, Tenant Isolation, and Transient Burst PRD
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary: This PRD defines product requirements for adding capacity guarantees and a controlled transient burst capability to Dedicated (reserved) capacity. The goal is to let customers purchase and observe firm throughput/latency guarantees while providing a limited, auditable burst window to absorb traffic spikes without sacrificing noisy-neighbor protections or cross-tenant safety.

Background: Customers buying Dedicated capacity expect predictable throughput and isolation. Currently reserved pools provide baseline capacity but lack a formalized burst mechanism and explicit isolation guarantees (soft vs hard isolation, preemption semantics, QoS tiers). Several enterprise customers requested the ability to tolerate short peak windows (e.g., 1–10 minutes) while maintaining billing and observability that differentiates guaranteed vs best-effort traffic. This PRD balances economics (allowing better resource utilization) with reliability and predictable SLAs.
goals: Define capacity guarantee semantics for reserved pools (guaranteed RPS/tokens and latency SLOs).
Design a transient burst mechanism that allows controlled overcommit for short windows with clear preemption and billing rules.
Provide tenant isolation controls: hard isolation (physical exclusive GPUs) and soft isolation (shared GPUs with scheduler-enforced limits).
Expose configuration and observability in Redwood Console and API: per-route QoS, burst budgets, preemption logs, and cost attribution.
Ensure the runtime implements fair preemption and isolation without regressions to p50/p95 latency for guaranteed traffic.
Ship an operator-friendly rollout with canary and opt-in by customer pools, plus acceptance tests and chaos scenarios.
non_goals: This PRD does not change pricing model for hosted API customers.
We will not implement automatic cross-customer bursting across regions in the first iteration.
This scope excludes a full metering rewrite — we will extend existing usage records with burst-specific tags.
user_stories: As a platform admin, I want to create Reserved Pools that guarantee 200 rps and allow a 5-minute burst window to 400 rps so my service survives traffic spikes.
As an SRE, I want clear preemption logs that show which requests were evicted or deprioritized during burst windows, so I can troubleshoot customer incidents.
As an engineering manager, I want the Console to show burst budget remaining and cost delta if burst is used, so I can make trade-offs before approving longer bursts.
As a tenant with strict compliance, I want the option for hard isolation (dedicated GPUs) to ensure no co-located workloads can affect my SLAs.
requirements: API: Create/Update Reserved Pool with fields: guaranteed_capacity (tokens/sec), min_capacity, max_capacity, burst_window_seconds, burst_multiplier, isolation_mode (hard|soft), preemption_policy (none|graceful|aggressive).
Runtime: Honor guaranteed_capacity at all times for traffic marked 'guaranteed'.

Runtime: Support burst windows that allow short-term capacity up to guaranteed_capacity * burst_multiplier for a configured burst_window_seconds, enforced by token-bucket on pool-level and per-tenant QoS tags.

Billing/Usage: Tag all consumed tokens during burst windows and surface a 'burst_consumption' metric in usage exports; costs are billed at existing per-token rates but with an optional surcharge flag for enterprise managers.
Isolation: Hard isolation must map to dedicated GPU allocations with no tenant co-location; soft isolation must provide scheduler-enforced caps and preferential queuing for guaranteed traffic.

Preemption: Define deterministic preemption ordering: (1) best-effort traffic, (2) non-guaranteed queued requests, (3) degradeable model variants. Provide graceful preemptions with TTL hints and 503-with-retry headers when appropriate.
Observability: Console and API must show per-pool: guaranteed_capacity, current_utilization, burst_budget_remaining, last_preemption_events (with request ids), and cost_delta_if_bursted.

SLOs: During and after burst events, guaranteed traffic p95 latency must not degrade by more than 20% vs baseline for pools configured with isolation_mode=hard. For soft isolation, degradation must be documented and accepted thresholds set per-customer.
acceptance_criteria: Provisioning: Create a Reserved Pool via API and Console with guaranteed_capacity=1000 tokens/min and burst_multiplier=2 and verify values persist and are shown in Console.
Guaranteed SLA: Run a synthetic workload to saturate guaranteed_capacity; guaranteed traffic maintains p95 latency within 10% of baseline for hard isolation pools over a 30-minute window.
Burst behavior: Trigger a 3-minute spike to 2x capacity; verify that burst_budget is consumed, burst tokens are recorded in usage export, and best-effort traffic is preempted first.
Preemption logs: During burst-induced preemptions, Console shows at least one preemption event with request ids and reason; SRE can correlate to request telemetry in tracing.
Billing export: Usage export contains burst_consumption tag and matches Console cost_delta estimation within 5% for the test scenario.

Isolation modes: For a hard isolation pool, validate no co-located tenants appear on host-level metrics during a stress test. For soft isolation, validate scheduler-enforced caps reduce best-effort throughput before guaranteed throughput.
Security: Key management and audit logs include pool creation and modifications and have entries for burst policy changes (security_review_required=true).
metrics: Number and duration of burst events per pool
Cost delta (projected vs actual) attributable to burst consumption
Customer-reported incidents tied to burst events
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): Implement API + runtime changes behind a feature flag; onboard 3 internal alpha customers and run controlled spike exercises.
Phase 2 (Early Access): Open opt-in to 10 enterprise customers; expose Console controls and detailed billing tags; monitor for regressions for 4 weeks.
Phase 3 (General Availability): Gradual enablement for new Dedicated purchases, user education, and updated SLA docs; automated tests and runbook published.
Backout plan: Feature flag off will revert burst allowance and preserve existing guaranteed capacity. Preemption logs and usage tags remain available for post-mortem.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Burst feature could enable noisy neighbors that impact other customers. Mitigation: default burst multiplier small (<=2), require explicit opt-in for soft isolation, and enforce preemption ordering that protects guaranteed traffic.
Risk: Billing disputes due to burst consumption. Mitigation: provide simulated cost preview in Console and clear 'burst_consumption' tags in exports; offer 30-day dispute window for early customers.
Risk: Complexity in scheduler causes regressions. Mitigation: ship runtime changes behind a flag and require performance benchmarks (no >5% regression on baseline p95 for guaranteed flows).
Risk: Security/audit gaps when modifying pool policies. Mitigation: require role-based permission to change burst settings and ensure KMS/HSM audit entries for related operations.
open_questions: Should burst billing include an explicit surcharge or rely on existing per-token prices?
What is the recommended default burst_window_seconds for typical enterprise workloads (1m, 5m, 10m)?
Do we need a 'soft preemption' mode that first attempts to switch to lower-cost quantized models before evicting requests?
How should multi-region Dedicated pools behave when region-level capacity differs?
